body:
Are you sure it's really unlimited for the user that runs the server and not for an other user ?

I have stressed netty with millions of requests and had no problems.

---

Norman Maurer
nmaurer@redhat.com

JBoss, by Red Hat

Am 15.07.2013 um 11:32 schrieb tomassommar notifications@github.com:

> unlimited
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub.

When running ulimit -a, I could se that -n (file descriptors) was set to 1024. When changing this value to 65536, the server ran through the requests as expected. Thus, it seems that the ulimit could have been the problem. Thank you for pointing me in the right direction.

However, when stressing the server and running "lsof | grep java | wc -l" to count the number of active connections repeatedly, I can see that the number of active connection climbs up to arount 3500 before dropping down to around 500. Is this normal? >3000 open connections seem to indicate that connections are kept open for quite some time.

On another note, should'nt this be handled by netty? If the server runs out of available connections, rather than the server crashing, should'nt it queue or block incomming calls untill the server is ready to process them?
You are correct, it should continue accepting the incoming connection instead of closing itself.

I updated to the latest 4.0.2.Final-SNAPSHOT. Now the server doesnt crash, but neither does it seem to handle the connections appropriately. The server doesnt respond and logs the same following exception:

```
2013-07-17 12:31:37 WARN  DefaultChannelPipeline:953 - An exceptionCaught() event was fired, and it reached at the tail of the pipeline. It usually means the last handler in the pipeline did not handle the exception.
java.io.IOException: Too many open files
        at sun.nio.ch.ServerSocketChannelImpl.accept0(Native Method)
        at sun.nio.ch.ServerSocketChannelImpl.accept(ServerSocketChannelImpl.java:152)
        at io.netty.channel.socket.nio.NioServerSocketChannel.doReadMessages(NioServerSocketChannel.java:111)
        at io.netty.channel.nio.AbstractNioMessageChannel$NioMessageUnsafe.read(AbstractNioMessageChannel.java:70)
        at io.netty.channel.nio.NioEventLoop.processSelectedKey(NioEventLoop.java:497)
        at io.netty.channel.nio.NioEventLoop.processSelectedKeysOptimized(NioEventLoop.java:465)
        at io.netty.channel.nio.NioEventLoop.run(NioEventLoop.java:359)
        at io.netty.util.concurrent.SingleThreadEventExecutor$2.run(SingleThreadEventExecutor.java:101)
        at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:662)
```

So it seems that the server is now accepting incoming connections, but they aren't getting handled.

The server is not accepting these connections; it is attempting to, but is hitting the ulimit.  Instead of this causing the server to shutdown, it just causes this error to be propagated along your channel pipeline.  If sufficient connections disconnect, dropping the number of open files below the ulimit, does this error still get thrown?
If the number of connections are under the ulimit the error is not thrown. However,  shoudln't new connections get queued and processed rather than an error being thrown?

issue.title: Resurfaced "java.io.IOException: Too many open files" when hit by multiple requests issue

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
This has previously been reported in issue 1578: https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/1578 

The issue was set as resolved in 4.0.2.Final, but now exists in 4.0.6.Final.

Do you have any advice on this issue?
